experiments.goal: Certified projector-free bound for the near-band coupling M(s) = C 1_(-inf,s](A) C^T at varying spectral cutoff s (review revision-2 move 3).
experiments.method: DERIVED majorant M(s) <= C Phi_k C^T with Phi_k = ((bI - A)/(b - s))^(2^k), k exact Arb squarings of the enclosed native A; certified trace and lambda_max upper bounds; response bound C A^-1 Phi_k C^T where A >= aI is certified.
experiments.result: Certified at L = 4, 5, 6 (both parities) for s = eps + 1e-8, 1e-6, 1e-4, 1e-2. At s = eps + 1e-6 the certified trace bounds are 1.7e-6 / 2.0e-6 (L=4), 3.6e-6 / 4.9e-6 (L=5) and 9.2e-6 / 5.9e-6 (L=6); they grow with s (to 1.4e-2 - 6.2e-2 at s = eps + 1e-2). The bound is resolution-limited (recorded per row), so it bounds M(s + resolution) rather than M(s) sharply.

experiments.goal: Does small near-band coupling discriminate positive from negative pencils (review move 3, falsification)?
experiments.method: S1: rank-one negative term in the low block (C, A unchanged). S2: two adjacent actual zeros merged into an off-line quartet 1/2 +- delta +- i gamma_mid in the explicit-formula representation of the native form (mode transform calibrated on the pole channel; zero sum reproduces the native form at L=2). Native and synthetic pencils compared at one common tolerance below the detection threshold.
experiments.result: Not discriminating. S1 is certified negative with identical C and A. In the low band at every state the synthetic pencil is certified negative while its certified coupling bound agrees with the native one within 5% (0.004-4.3%). A high-band quartet makes A itself indefinite; at the split, coupling responds only at L=6 (1.2e-2 against 9e-6). The detection threshold eps*(delta) is quadratic in delta for small delta with c(L) = 9.4, 17.9, 28.2 (low band); the eps = 1/2 and 1/3 checkpoints are blind to delta = 1/10 quartets, the eps = 1/4 checkpoint at L=6 detects them (as predicted in session before the L6 run).

experiments.goal: Investigate the full signed source -arch - prime jointly at the native checkpoint states (review revision-2 move 4; work package F).
experiments.method: signed_source.py on the E-D1 slices (full Gram): channel energies along the slice spectrum, restrictions to the near-null subspace V, a prime-cutoff sweep up to Q = floor(e^L), per-prime-power contributions at the bottom vector, certified truncated-prime witnesses (L = 4, 5) and the DERIVED family comparison.
experiments.result: On V (dimension 51/50, 142/141, 346/345) the two channels are each indefinite with O(1) eigenvalues (-arch in [-2.1, 5.4]) and cancel to a joint form in [-5e-15, 7.5e-3]. -arch alone is certified not positive at L = 4, 5. Positivity appears only at the full prime cell: dropping only the largest prime power is certified negative at L = 4, 5 and floating-negative at L = 6. At the bottom vector the archimedean budget 2.0-3.0 is consumed by the prime atoms with little internal cancellation. No decomposition into independently controlled native terms was found.
